title: Jack Draper withdraws from Wimbledon with recurrence of left arm injury
content:
THE ALL ENGLAND CLUB, London — Jack Draper, the most high-profile male British player at this year’s Wimbledon, has joined his female counterpart Emma Raducanu in pulling out of the tournament due to injury.

He withdrew, citing a recurrence of the bone bruising in his left, playing arm, ahead of facing American No. 6 seed Taylor Fritz in a blockbuster first-round match scheduled for Tuesday.

Draper, 24, wrote on social media Monday afternoon: “Devastated to share that I have had to withdraw from my first round match due to a recurrence of my arm injury. There have been a lot of painful moments in the last 12 months but this one is definitely the absolute worst as there is no greater honour for a British player than playing at Wimbledon. I will continue to persevere through this. Thank you for the support!!”

The news followed Raducanu announcing Sunday night that a stress fracture in her right leg had forced her to withdraw from the tournament, and a first-round match against Antonia Ružić.

Draper was out with the original arm injury from August last year until February, and after a brief return was forced out for a couple of months with a knee problem. This is another bitter blow for a player who was ranked No. 4 this time last year but has tumbled out of the world’s top 100 because of those persistent injuries.

Draper described the initial arm injury he suffered last year as “extremely complicated” in a news conference Sunday.

“It’s one of those, it’s hard to tell when you can push, when not to push.”

Draper also discussed the mental toll of his persistent injuries, which have dogged him on and off for the last few years, and spoke about working with a sports psychologist.

“You have something that stops you in your tracks when you’re not expecting it. I think it’s really difficult to accept that, especially after coming through what you’ve come through in the past,” he said.

Draper also discussed the landscape in men’s tennis, with Carlos Alcaraz, Lorenzo Musetti, Holger Rune and Arthur Fils other top young men’s players sidelined by injury.

“When I look at the draws for the weeks when I was out, everything is shoulder, arm, wrist. They need to really take a close look at what we’re doing on tour. Definitely the state of the (ATP) Masters 1000s, the 12-day events,” he said.

Dusan Lajović of Serbia will replace Draper in the draw against Fritz.

British players exiting a tournament early has long been a running joke in the sport, but losing the two country’s two biggest names before Wimbledon has even started? That’s rough luck by anyone’s standards.

Wimbledon is such a huge event that it doesn’t live or die on the success of the home players — which is good given how rare success for them has tended to be — but it’s still a big blow so early on. Draper and Raducanu are far and away the most high-profile players in the singles draws, and a run for a British player has always been one of the most effective ways to bring casual fans into the sport. For the BBC, there’ll no doubt be disappointment at losing these two, especially in the post-Andy Murray age.

Once again it’s Cameron Norrie, the men’s No. 26 seed in action against Michael Zheng Monday, who’s likely to be the last Brit standing. But despite semifinal and quarterfinal appearances here previously, he’s never had much cut through with the British public.

Leaving aside these parochial concerns, Draper’s ongoing injury issues do, as he said, highlight how many young, exciting players on the ATP Tour are currently sidelined. Aneke Rune, the mother of Holger, one such player, recently called this out too as her son continues his rehabilitation after eight months out with a ruptured Achilles tendon.

Whatever the root causes, Draper is long overdue some good luck when it comes to injuries.
